text: A business makes money from customers. And customers come from marketing.
So every marketing decision is one question: where does the next dollar go?
Conferences, billboards, Google Ads, LinkedIn, S.E.O. Each with its own language, and its own clock.
So we pick by gut, or by the easiest number. LinkedIn: cheapest leads, pricey customers.
First principles: put every channel in one currency. Cost per qualified sales lead.
Ask what the next dollar buys. Move money in small steps. Measure. Repeat weekly.
In Snowflake, one agent per channel reads only its own data. A C.M.O. agent allocates.
Numbers come from S.Q.L., never the model. Small moves, it makes alone. Big ones go to the C.E.O., with evidence.
Move fourteen thousand from LinkedIn to conferences? Approve. Six percent more qualified leads, same budget.
Agentic C.M.O. The C.E.O. steers. The agent runs marketing.
